title: Chicken and Sweetcorn Pie
subtitle: A creamy chicken filling with sweetcorn under a puff pastry lid
excerpt: Tender chicken thighs and sweet tinned sweetcorn in a thick cream sauce, topped with a golden puff pastry lid.
sourceNotes: British family pie tradition, using boneless chicken thighs for flavour and ease.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the filling separately. Add the pastry lid fresh before baking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling a day ahead. Add the pastry lid and bake when ready.

content.text: A simple pie with a creamy filling and a crisp pastry lid on top. Chicken thighs stay juicy in the sauce; breast meat tends to dry out. Cool the filling a little before topping with pastry so the lid puffs up properly in the oven.
Melt the butter in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken pieces and cook for 5 minutes, turning once, until lightly coloured.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually pour in the stock, stirring to get rid of any lumps.
Add the cream and sweetcorn. Simmer gently for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick. Season well. Leave to cool for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200C. Pour the filling into the pie dish.
Lay the puff pastry over the top, trim to fit and press the edges onto the dish. Brush with beaten egg and cut two slits in the top.
Bake for 25 minutes until the pastry is puffed and deep gold. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The pastry lid sinks into the filling.
items.cause: The filling was too hot when the pastry was placed on top.
items.fix: Cool the filling for at least 15 minutes. It should be warm, not steaming.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and watery.
items.cause: The flour was not cooked enough, or the stock was added too quickly.
items.fix: Cook the flour for a full minute before adding stock. Add the stock in three stages, stirring after each.

items.symptom: The pastry is brown on top but raw underneath.
items.cause: The filling was too deep and transferred too much steam.
items.fix: Use a wide, shallow pie dish so the filling sits in a thinner layer.
